- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to underestimate prices; apply upward bias correction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00), especially in early forecast horizon; cap or dampen peak forecasts.
- Forecasts show strong mean reversion bias — if price deviates >1.5σ from recent 7-day average, adjust toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; reduce forecast volatility if sentiment is volatile or noisy.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +0.00 or flat sentiment, model tends to drift toward extreme values; apply smoothing or decay filter to prevent runaway forecasts.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often undercorrects — increase downward adjustment by 10–20% of forecast magnitude.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overcorrects — reduce upward adjustment by 10–20% of forecast magnitude.
